reading.title: A Story from History
reading.text: This is a fictional story about two kingdoms, Arden and Belmor. For many years the kingdoms lived in peace, but a quarrel about land grew bigger. Finally, the king of Belmor declared war. War broke out, and many people had to leave their homes. The war lasted five years, and both sides lost many people. In the end, the two kings met to talk, and they agreed to end the war. Today there is a war memorial in the capital of Arden, where schoolchildren lay flowers every year. Teachers say that the story reminds us how important it is to solve problems without fighting.

reading.title: Peace Day at School
reading.text: Every September our school celebrates Peace Day. This year, the pupils made posters about world peace and sang songs about living in peace. Our headteacher told us that peace is more than just the end of war. It means that people respect one another and find peaceful solutions to disagreements. In the afternoon, two classes that had been arguing about the football pitch made peace. They shook hands and agreed to share the pitch. After that, we planted a small tree to remember the day. I think it is the quietest and happiest day of the school year.

reading.title: The Castle on the Hill
reading.text: In this old story, a castle stands on a hill above the river town of Lorne. One autumn night, an enemy army launched a surprise attack on the town. The people ran to the castle for safety, and the guards closed the gates. The castle was under attack for three days, but the walls were strong. Then the lord of the castle decided to try a different plan. He sent a message offering to talk. The enemy leader agreed, and the attack stopped without more fighting. Today visitors can walk around the castle and imagine how the town survived.

reading.title: The Bus Strike
reading.text: In the city of Redford, bus drivers went on strike last week. They were in a pay dispute with the bus company. The drivers said their wages had not risen for three years. The union held a strike ballot, and most workers voted to take strike action. For three days, the city was very quiet. Many people walked or cycled to work, and some schools started later. On the fourth day, both sides met to settle the dispute. They agreed on a small pay rise and shorter shifts. The union called off the strike, and the buses were back on the road the next morning.

reading.title: Saving the Library
reading.text: When the council said it would close our local library, the neighbourhood started a campaign. A campaign group launched a petition, and over two thousand people signed it. Hundreds of demonstrators marched through the streets with signs that said Save Our Library. The mayor listened to the crowd and promised to look at the plan again. A week later, the council announced that the library would stay open. The campaign group thanked everyone who had taken part.
